articles.title: X Money will be the only payout option for U.S. creators
articles.summary: X has made its new X Money payments platform the mandatory payout method for U.S. creators enrolled in its Original Content Rewards and Subscriptions programs, effective immediately, with no alternative option offered domestically. X says the switch lets creators access funds instantly upon payment rather than waiting to hit a payout threshold. To qualify, creators must verify their phone number for an X Money account and maintain an X Premium subscription—already a monetization requirement, so no added barrier there. Non-U.S. creators will keep using Stripe for payouts. X Money, launched in beta in November 2025, is powered by Cross River Bank, which also issues its Visa debit card for ATM withdrawals, after X secured a regulatory agreement to overcome state-level pushback tied to its Middle East ownership ties. The move comes as TechCrunch reports a rise in hacking attempts targeting X accounts specifically to steal X Money payment details, adding security pressure as X pushes toward becoming an all-in-one "everything app."
articles.li_summary: X now requires all U.S. creators in its Original Content Rewards and Subscriptions programs to receive payouts exclusively through X Money, its Cross River Bank-powered payment platform launched in beta November 2025.

articles.title: TikTok signs multi-year NFL deal
articles.summary: TikTok has signed a new multi-year partnership with the NFL to deepen the league's presence on the platform through expanded content and interactive fan features. The deal introduces NFL game day hubs built on TikTok's GamePlan sports partnership framework, giving fans a dedicated space to browse trending clips, complete fan challenges for exclusive rewards, and engage around live game moments. TikTok will also host more highlights, archival footage, and ongoing storytelling content from the league and its 32 teams throughout the year. Brands get a new avenue too, with advertisers able to leverage NFL-related trends via TikTok's Pulse Premiere ad product. TikTok says posts tagged #NFL rose more than 32% over the past year, and cites earlier research showing 59% of its users find watching sports content on the app more entertaining than watching live games, signaling why leagues are prioritizing the platform for fan engagement.
articles.li_summary: TikTok and the NFL signed a multi-year deal adding GamePlan-powered game day hubs, fan challenges, highlights and Pulse Premiere ads, after #NFL posts grew over 32% in the past year.
